newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money mostly unchanged at 3.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money mostly unchanged at 3.10 pct.

text.p: German call money traded virtually unchanged from Thursday's levels on Friday even as conditions tightened slightly before the weekend.
"Generally we are trading on the same levels as on Thursday," one dealer said. Rates began the day trading near 3.07/08 percent and then climbed to around 3.10 percent, the levels seen on Thursday.
Although holdings at the Bundesbank eased slightly, dealers still said that overall liquidity remained largely in equilibrium.
Dealers also said the federal government was adding funds into the market which helped rates at relatively low levels.
Banks' daily holdings in interest-free accounts at the Bundesbank stood at 41.0 billion marks on Thursday compared with 42.3 billion marks one day earlier.

The monthly average rate however nudged slightly higher to 40.3 billion marks from 40.2 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were negligible. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.11633 percent on Friday compared with 3.11900 percent on Thursday.
